prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1490; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured vehicle reportedly backed into a parked sedan while exiting a space. Claimant reports a wrist injury from the impact and states she was seated in her vehicle at the time. Photos requested from both parties.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. She reports a wrist fracture confirmed at urgent care and is awaiting follow-up imaging. She is not represented by an attorney and says she is handling the claim herself. Explained the general claims process and that she may request a copy of the police or incident report.

Entry 3: Received photos from insured showing rear bumper contact on the insured vehicle and a dented rear door on the claimant vehicle. Damage appears consistent with the reported mechanism. Estimate requested from the repair shop for the claimant vehicle. Medical authorization form sent to claimant for records review.

Entry 4: Claimant returned signed medical authorization. Records received from urgent care show diagnosis of a wrist fracture with splint applied and referral to orthopedics. Reviewed records with supervisor. No prior claims found on claimant's file for the same body part. Requested orthopedic consult notes when available.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant to confirm status of treatment. She reports orthopedic visit is scheduled and she has been out of work for part of the period. Advised her to keep receipts for all out-of-pocket medical and wage-related expenses. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect injury component. File remains open pending orthopedic records and repair estimate.
